reason: The hypothesis relies on general knowledge that alumina is an oxygen barrier, but the cited passages provide no specific prior evidence that an alumina coating has been successfully applied to HfNbTaTiZr or that it prevents embrittlement while preserving mechanical properties. E2 only mentions that anti-oxidation coatings are 'still required', which is a statement of need, not evidence of efficacy.
premises: Alumina coatings can act as effective oxygen diffusion barriers on refractory alloys at high temperatures.
The coating will remain adherent and continuous on HfNbTaTiZr during exposure at ~1000 °C in air.
Preventing oxygen ingress will preserve the alloy's intrinsic ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
The cited evidence explicitly recommends anti-oxidation coatings for HfNbTaTiZr-type alloys for high-temperature air use.
